preamble: Progressive nasal assimilation turns the [d] of a cluster [nd] into [n], giving geminate [nn]. It is a regular change in central and southern Italian dialects, so Latin quandō 'when' and mundus 'world' are Neapolitan quanno and munno.

examples.note: The [d] of the cluster [nd] assimilates to the preceding nasal, giving geminate [nn].

sources: Campbell, L. (2013). Historical Linguistics: An Introduction (3rd ed.). Edinburgh University Press; MIT Press. https://lccn.loc.gov/2012038044
